answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it pays the walnut fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the oasis ledger attributes every share, the cedar audit exposes the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 55% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 22 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
